title: A Madcap
checks: No points of issue known: no bibliography or dealer gives first-edition points for this book

The story ran as a serial in Cassell's Little Folks in 1904; book editions found are Grosset & Dunlap, New York, 1904 (red decorated cloth, illustrated frontispiece), an undated Cassell edition, an undated Hurst & Co. (New York) edition and a Ward Lock 1906 edition (dealer listings)
Title page: note the publisher. Cassell, London, undated is the likeliest British first, but no source confirms it (uncertain)
One undated Cassell-headed listing describes brown decorated cloth with a colour frontispiece and colour plates, 260 pages (one dealer; the listing also mentions Hurst & Co., so uncertain)
Any list of other L. T. Meade titles in the back or on the endpapers: titles from after 1904 would show a later printing (general method, not confirmed for this book)
her_copy_hint: Hers is undated, which fits the Cassell edition (Cassell did not date it). Check the publisher on the title page and whether there is a colour frontispiece, but no source can confirm a first from the book alone.

title: A Tale of Two Cities
checks: Title page of the first: 'London: Chapman and Hall, 1859', dated (Bauman Rare Books). An undated copy is not the first
First issue: page 213 misnumbered '113' (Bauman Rare Books and other dealers)
First issue: a signature letter 'b' printed on the List of Plates page (Bauman Rare Books)
16 etched plates by H. K. Browne ('Phiz'), including the frontispiece and engraved title (Bauman; another dealer counts frontispiece, vignette title and 14 plates, which is the same 16)
It was also issued in 8 monthly parts (June to December 1859) in wrappers; some firsts are bound up from these parts (Bauman)
Original cloth colour of the first: one listing says maroon (uncertain)
her_copy_hint: Her note 'Undated, after 1870' rules out the first (1859, dated). Note the publisher and illustrator on the title page to date it; page 213 numbered correctly confirms a later printing.

title: A World of Girls
checks: Title page of the first: Cassell, 1886, 288 pages, with drawings by M. E. Edwards (Orlando bibliography)

Cassell's early printings carry the year and an edition or 'thousand' line, e.g. a '4th ed.' dated 1888 'with original drawings by M. E. Edwards' (Open Library) and the 21st thousand by 1894 (National Library of Ireland). A 'thousand' or edition line means a reprint

A Cassell printing of 1892 has 8 drawings by M. E. Edwards (National Library of Ireland); later Cassell printings have four colour plates by Gertrude A. Steel instead. Steel plates mean a later printing
Dealers date undated Cassell copies to about 1904-1910 (one brown cloth copy 'ca. 1910'), so an undated copy is probably a later printing (inference from dealer listings, uncertain)
No other points of issue known
her_copy_hint: Hers is undated, while the 1886 first and the early reprints carry a date, so it is most likely a later Cassell printing. Look at who drew the pictures: Gertrude A. Steel colour plates would confirm a later one.

title: Andersen's Fairy Tales
checks: No points of issue apply: the first collection was published in Danish in Copenhagen (C. A. Reitzel, 1835-37), and English selections came from many publishers from the 1840s on
An undated English selection can only be dated from the publisher's name and address, the translator and the illustrator on the title page, and any adverts in the back (general method)
her_copy_hint: Hers is undated, so it cannot be a first. Note the publisher, translator and illustrator on the title page; those are what would date it.

title: Brer Rabbit's a Rascal
checks: Back of the dust wrapper: a first lists exactly 12 titles, numbered 1 to 12. A wrapper listing 13 or more titles is a later printing (Enid Blyton Society)
Dates printed inside Dean books don't help. The Society says they 'are irrelevant and will not help identify a 1st edition', so a missing date proves nothing either way
Without the wrapper: the Society gives no other point, so a first can't be confirmed from the book alone
Publisher Dean & Son, 1965; illustrated by Grace Lodge; No. 10 in Dean's Reward Series (Society)
Boards: red, with black title on the spine (one dealer, Stella Books)
A second dealer also describes a 1965 Dean Blyton first as having 'just 12 titles listed on the back of the dust-wrapper', which backs up the Society's rule (one dealer, Biblio)
Later printings exist: Dean 1995 and Egmont 2007. Check that it says Dean & Son and credits Grace Lodge
Price printed on the wrapper: not found in any source
her_copy_hint: Her 'Undated' doesn't count against it, because Dean books aren't dated reliably. Look at the back of the dust wrapper first and count the numbered titles: 12 means first edition.

title: Black Beauty
checks: Title page of the first: 'Black Beauty: His Grooms and Companions. The Autobiography of a Horse', London: Jarrold and Sons, 1877, dated (Jonkers; ABAA)
Frontispiece engraved after C. Hewitt (Jonkers)
Eight pages of publisher's adverts at the end (one auction listing, Sotheby's)

Binding: Carter's variants A and B are the only certain first-issue bindings (gilt or black horse's head and border); variant C is 'comparatively common' (Jonkers, quoting Carter). Cloth colours reported: green, brown, terracotta, blue (dealers disagree)
Original price 2/- in cloth boards, 2/6 in extra boards with gilt edges (Jonkers)
her_copy_hint: Hers is undated, and the first is dated 1877 on the title page, so it is a later printing. The publisher's name and address, and any adverts, are what would date it.

title: Captain of Two Schools
checks: Imprint: 'Frederick Warne & Co. Ltd, 1950' (one dealer, AbeBooks)
Red cloth boards, 256 pages, colour illustrated frontispiece with no artist named (one dealer, AbeBooks)
One seller tags H. M. Brock as the artist (not confirmed anywhere; uncertain)
No points of issue known: no bibliography or dealer gives first-edition points, a wrapper price or a title list
her_copy_hint: Her 1950 matches the only dated edition found. If the imprint page says 1950 with no reprint line, it is very probably the first, but no source gives anything more to check.

title: China Fights Back
checks: Title page: Victor Gollancz, London, 1938; subtitle 'An American Woman with the Eighth Route Army' (library catalogues)
Cover: the words 'Left Book Club edition' (Japanese union catalogue, CiNii)
286 pages and 1 map, by J. F. Horrabin (Swiss and French library records)

Binding: red paper-covered boards (one dealer, Jonkers). From 1938 the Club's books were in a red stiff binding, replacing the earlier orange limp covers marked 'Left Book Club Edition. Not for sale to the public' (Sheffield University archive)
There was also a 1938 New York edition (Vanguard Press); the London Left Book Club issue is the British first (dealer listing)
Whether Gollancz also issued a separate trade edition of this title was not found (uncertain)
her_copy_hint: Her note 'Left Book Club Edition' and her year 1938 fit the first British edition. Check the cover wording, the 1938 date with no reprint line, and the Horrabin map.

title: Claudine at St Clare's
checks: Imprint page: should give only Methuen 1944, with no later edition or reprint dates after it. Methuen reprints of this series carry their own later dates (e.g. a 1953 printing) (dealers)
Illustrated by W. Lindsay Cable; the wrapper is a pictorial wrapper, also by Lindsay Cable (Society; Jonkers)
Cloth: one dealer says red cloth with a blue line drawing (Jonkers); another says pink cloth with dark titles and a vignette (Stella Books) (uncertain: dealers disagree, possibly a faded red)
A 1953 printing has red boards with black lettering and vignette (one dealer, Stella). Black lettering may point to a reprint (uncertain)
The Society page gives no points for the first and doesn't name its cover artist
Price printed on the wrapper: not found
her_copy_hint: Her year 1944 matches the first. Check the imprint page (back of the title page) for any date after 1944, then look at the cloth and the colour of the lettering.

title: Corridors of Power
checks: Imprint: Macmillan, London, 1964 (UK first; the US edition is Scribner, New York)

Imprint page: any 'Reprinted' line means a later printing (general practice; no source quotes the exact wording on this book)
No other points of issue known
her_copy_hint: Her 1964 matches the Macmillan first, and she has a question mark. Check the back of the title page for any reprint line, the red cloth, and, if there's a wrapper, the Sidney Nolan design with 25s net.

title: Fifth Formers of St Clare's
checks: Imprint page: Methuen 1945 and nothing later. The 2nd impression is dated 1947 and the 4th 1949 (dealers), so any later date means a reprint
Cloth: yellow, with the Lindsay Cable picture stamped in red (Jonkers). The 1947 and 1949 reprints are also yellow cloth (Stella; Biblio), so the cloth alone doesn't prove a first
Line drawings by W. Lindsay Cable (Society; Jonkers)

Price printed on the wrapper: not found. Both dealer firsts with wrappers were price-clipped
The Society page gives no points for the first
her_copy_hint: Her 1945 matches the first. The imprint page is the deciding check: '1945' alone is the first; a 1947 or 1949 line means a later impression in the same yellow cloth.

title: Five Go to Mystery Moor
checks: Imprint page: Hodder & Stoughton, London, 1954, with no impression or reprint line after it. Later printings do exist; one dealer lists a 'Fifth Impression' of 1960 that still says 'First published in 1954'
Wrapper, front flap: the price should be '7/6 net', not clipped (two dealers)
Endpapers: pictures by Eileen A. Soper. The Society shows the first-edition endpapers and wrapper, both by Soper
Text illustrations by Eileen A. Soper, several of them full-page (dealer description of a later impression; no count found)
Size: about 190 x 130 mm (one dealer, Shapero; from a search snippet only)
Cloth colour of the first printing: not confirmed. The 1960 fifth impression is red cloth lettered in black (one dealer) (uncertain for the first)
No list of titles on the wrapper or flaps, and no 'last title listed' point, was found for this book
her_copy_hint: Her copy says 1954 and she notes 'First edition', so look first at the back of the title page for any 'second impression' or 'reprinted' line, then at the wrapper flap for an unclipped 7/6 net price.

title: Five Go to Smuggler's Top
checks: Imprint: Hodder & Stoughton, 1945. One auction house describes the first impression as 'London: Hodder & Stoughton Limited, July 1945', so look for a 1945 date (possibly with 'July') and no reprint lines after it (exact wording uncertain)
Later printings exist: one dealer lists a 1948 second impression, and the Society's first reprint entry is 1951

Frontispiece in colour, plus many black-and-white drawings by Eileen A. Soper, some printed in red or blue and black (Tooveys)
Endpapers: pictures by Soper; the Society's review says they show George climbing down a wall by a rope ladder
About 8 x 5 inches, 192 pages (one dealer)

Wrapper flap: Stella & Rose's research says the true first-edition wrapper spells 'Anne' correctly on the front flap; a variant wrapper misspells it (from a search snippet; the article itself could not be opened)
The Society shows only a 1954 wrapper for this title, not the first-edition one
No list-of-titles point was found
her_copy_hint: Her copy says 1945 and she notes 'First edition', which fits. Check the back of the title page for reprint lines, then look for blue cloth, the rope-ladder endpaper, and 6/- net on the wrapper.

title: Five Have a Mystery to Solve

No list-of-titles point was found
her_copy_hint: Her copy says 1962 and she notes 'First edition'. Look for red cloth with black lettering, picture endpapers, and no 'impression' line on the back of the title page.

title: Five on a Secret Trail
checks: Imprint: Hodder & Stoughton, London, 1956, with no later impression line. Later impressions exist; a search snippet mentions a third impression of about 1962

182 pages (one dealer)
Wrapper: by Soper. Price '7s 6d net' on the inside front flap (one seller, from a search snippet)
No list-of-titles point was found
her_copy_hint: Her copy says 1956 and she notes 'First edition'. Check the back of the title page for any 'second' or 'third impression' line, then look for red cloth and 7/6 net on the flap.

title: Go Ahead, Secret Seven
checks: Reprints carry dated lines: one dealer quotes 'First published 1953, second impression 1953', and a 1957 fifth printing exists. A first should show 1953 with no impression line after it

About 128 pages (one dealer)

her_copy_hint: Her copy has no year, yet later impressions seem to print 'First published 1953' plus an impression line. Look carefully at the back of the title page and the last page for any date before assuming it is a first.

title: Philips' Universal Atlas
checks: No points of issue known: the first year of this title was not found. Library records found are for later editions (c1976, 1979, and a '4th edition, new ed.' of 1983)
Look on the title page or its back for an edition statement (e.g. '4th edition') and a date; atlases are usually dated by these and by the country borders on the maps (general method)
her_copy_hint: Her note says 'After 1934', presumably from something in the maps. An edition statement on the title page or its back would date it; there is nothing known that marks a first.

title: Practical Railway Working
checks: Title page of the first: 'Practical Railway Working' by Charles Travis, David R. Lamb and John A. Jenkinson, London: Boswell Printing and Publishing Co., 1915 (Harvard record via Open Library)
326 pages; a note 'Reprinted with additions from The Railway News' (Open Library)
Preface reportedly dated Marylebone Station, July 1915 (earlier research, one dealer; uncertain)
No later edition was found, so a 1915 Boswell copy is very probably the first (inference)
No points of issue known
her_copy_hint: Her 1915 matches the only edition found. Check that the publisher is Boswell, London, and that there's no 'second edition' line.

title: Sunday Times Travel and Holiday Guide
checks: The 1951 volume: 'The Sunday Times Travel and Holiday Guide to Great Britain, Northern Ireland, and the Republic of Ireland', edited by Leonard Russell and Elizabeth Nicholas, London: The Sunday Times, 591 pages; it 'superseded in part' the earlier Sunday Times Holiday Guide (National Library of Ireland)

No 1950 or earlier edition under this title was found, and a later new edition (team Vincent Cronin, Elizabeth Nicholas, Leonard Russell) was reviewed in 1966 (Spectator archive, via a search snippet). So 1951 is probably the first under this title (inference, uncertain)
No points of issue known
her_copy_hint: Her copy is 1951, which is the earliest edition found under this title. Check the editors (Russell and Nicholas) and the 591 pages to confirm it is the same edition.

title: The Island of Adventure
checks: Imprint: Macmillan and Co Ltd, London, 1944. A '1948' date or a 'second impression' line means a reprint (Lycanthia lists a first edition, second impression, 1948)
Binding: pictorial cloth (Jonkers, Rare and Antique Books); colour not given
327 pages (one dealer)
Illustrations in black and white by Stuart Tresilian; the wrapper is a wraparound picture by Tresilian (Society)

Beware the 1994 Macmillan facsimile of the first edition (Society reprint list)
No endpaper or list-of-titles point was found
her_copy_hint: She has '1944' with a question mark. If the back of the title page shows only 1944 and no impression or reprint line, it is likely a first. Also make sure it is not the 1994 facsimile.

title: The Model Railway Hobby
checks: No points of issue known, and the first year is not settled: Open Library and Trains.com give 1948 (Percival Marshall); a forum post says the first was 1949; copies dated 1943 are also listed (earlier research, Amazon)

Look on the title page and its back for the year and any edition or reprint line (general method)
her_copy_hint: Her copy says 1943, earlier than the 1948 and 1949 dates in catalogues. If 1943 is really printed in it, it may be an early edition, but no source confirms the first year; note exactly what the title page and its back say.

title: The Mountain of Adventure

Wraparound wrapper and illustrations by Stuart Tresilian (Society)
Keep apart from the Macmillan New York 1949 edition
No cloth colour, endpaper or list-of-titles point was found

Price printed on the wrapper: not found for either edition
